expectations_used.clarify: Pins the contract down from the visible suites instead of guessing — saying out loud that percent discounts floor to whole cents, that only the largest order-level percent applies, and that the rebate is judged on the amount owed after vouchers.
expectations_used.approach: Names a mechanism before typing: that ring_up runs three ordered stages (sku percents, then one order percent, then coupons tested against the running total), and that best_checkout has to search voucher-to-item pairings because a smaller discount can preserve the rebate.
expectations_used.communicate: Says which of the three parts they are on and which rule they are encoding as they encode it — announcing the move from bag_total's every-third-free arithmetic to ring_up's stage order, and stating the rebate trade-off in Part 3 out loud instead of working it out silently.
expectations_used.implement: Keeps every figure in integer cents with floor division, sorts sku promos by percent descending then code ascending, appends to the trail as each promo is applied rather than reconstructing it afterwards, and leaves the test files untouched.
expectations_used.verify: Hand-walks the stated examples before submitting — the 4100-cent cart through all three stages to 2458, and the 10000-cent rebate case where the voucher is better left unused — because each suite is graded once, at submit.
expectations_used.reflect: States which of the three parts they finished, names what is still shaky (for example the tie-break between equal-saving voucher assignments, or the skipped-coupon rule), and says what they would check next with more time.
